title: Sustainability: reduce, reuse and recycle
key_idea: Many of the Earth's resources are finite, so we should use less, reuse products and recycle materials. Recycling metals, glass and polymers saves raw materials, energy and landfill space, but materials must be collected and sorted first.

blocks.text: Humans use the Earth's resources for warmth, shelter, food and transport. This section covers the types of resource and what sustainable means.

items.meaning: A resource that is used up faster than it forms, so it will eventually run out. Crude oil and metal ores are examples.
A resource that can be replaced as it is used, such as wood from replanted trees.
Development that meets the needs of the current generation without compromising the needs of future generations.

items: Natural resources, supplemented by agriculture, provide food, timber, clothing and fuels.
Some natural products are supplemented or replaced by agricultural and synthetic products. Polymers can replace wood or wool.
Finite resources from the Earth, oceans and atmosphere are processed to provide energy and materials.

diagram.alt: Sort each resource into finite or renewable.

items: Finite resources will run out. Renewable resources can be replaced.
Sustainable development protects the needs of future generations.

blocks.text: Metals, glass, building materials, clay ceramics and most plastics come from limited raw materials. Using them less, or using them again, saves resources.

items: Reducing the use of materials cuts the use of raw materials and energy sources.
It also reduces waste and environmental impacts.
Getting raw materials by quarrying and mining causes environmental impacts.
Reuse
Recycle

values: The product is used again for the same job.
The material is made into a new product, often for a different use.
Glass bottles are washed and refilled.
Glass bottles are crushed and melted to make different glass products.

items: Metals are recycled by melting and recasting, or reforming into different products.
Scrap copper wire is heated until the copper melts, then recast into new products such as water pipes.
Some scrap steel is added to iron from a blast furnace. This reduces the amount of iron that needs to be extracted from iron ore.
The amount of separation needed depends on the material and the properties the final product needs.
Reduce and reuse save the most resources. Recycling makes materials into new products.
Metals are recycled by melting and recasting them.

blocks.text: Recycling is more sustainable than extracting new materials, but it is not free of problems.

items: It conserves finite raw materials such as metal ores.
It uses less energy than extracting the metal from its ore.
It produces less waste and uses less landfill.
It avoids the environmental impacts of mining and quarrying.
It causes fewer greenhouse gas emissions.
Materials must be collected and separated before they can be recycled.
Polymers must be sorted so they can be melted and reformed into a new product.
Polymers are made from crude oil, which is finite, and most are not biodegradable, so they persist in landfill.
Burning polymers for disposal produces gases that may be toxic.
Recycling conserves ores, saves energy and cuts waste.
Recycling needs collection and sorting, especially for polymers.
Polymers come from finite crude oil and last a long time in landfill.

checks.a: Development that meets the needs of the current generation without compromising the needs of future generations.

checks.q: Suggest two reasons why recycling scrap copper is more sustainable than extracting copper from its ore.
checks.a: Any two from: it uses less energy, it conserves copper ore, it produces less waste, it avoids the environmental impact of mining.

checks.q: Describe how scrap copper wire can be recycled to make new copper pipes.
checks.a: The wire is heated until the copper melts. The molten copper is recast or reformed into pipes.

checks.q: State two problems caused by the disposal of polymers.
checks.a: Any two from: they last a long time in landfill, they are not biodegradable, landfill sites fill up quickly, burning them produces toxic gases.

exam_phrases: meets needs of current generation without compromising needs of future generations

mistakes.wrong: Recycling is more sustainable because it is cheaper.
mistakes.right: References to cost are ignored. Give reasons such as less energy, conserves the ore, or less waste.

mistakes.wrong: Sustainable development means not harming or damaging the planet.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Say it meets the needs of the current generation without compromising the needs of future generations.

mistakes.wrong: Polymers are better than wood because they are renewable.
mistakes.right: Polymers are made from crude oil, which is finite. Their advantage is that they last a long time. Wood is the renewable material.

worked_example.question:
Copper can be obtained by:
• processing copper ores
• recycling scrap copper.

Suggest three reasons why recycling scrap copper is a more sustainable way of obtaining copper than processing copper ores.
answer_points: Recycling conserves copper ores, because copper ores are finite.
Recycling reduces waste, or reduces the use of landfill.
Mining and quarrying cause environmental impacts, which recycling avoids.
worked_example.tip: Any three score. References to cost are ignored.

exam_phrases: preserves ore reserves / ores are finite
less carbon dioxide / greenhouse gases emitted
polymers degrade very slowly / not biodegradable
(toxic) gases produced during disposal by combustion
trees can be regrown / wood is renewable

mistakes.wrong: Recycling is better for the environment because there is less pollution.
mistakes.right: Vague statements about the environment, pollution or sustainability are ignored. Give a specific point such as less carbon dioxide emitted or ores preserved.

mistakes.wrong: Recycling metals means less land is needed for mining.
mistakes.right: Less land used for mining, visual pollution and mining causing loss of habitat, noise or dust are ignored. Give preserves ore, uses less energy or less waste.
Cost arguments are ignored in these questions. Give a resource, energy or waste advantage.

worked_example.question:
This question is about the extraction of metals.

Give two advantages of obtaining metals by recycling rather than by extracting them from their metal ores.
answer_points: Any two from: preserves ore reserves, because ores are finite.
Uses less energy, or less electricity.
Less carbon dioxide or greenhouse gas is emitted.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each advantage, up to two. Cost arguments and vague statements about the environment are ignored.

exam_phrases: aluminium (metal) is sorted from other metals / materials
shredded or crushed into smaller pieces
molten aluminium is poured into moulds
recycling aluminium produces less greenhouse gas emissions

mistakes.right: References to electrolysis are not allowed. Recycling is sorting, shredding or crushing, melting, then pouring into moulds.

mistakes.wrong: Recycling aluminium needs 14 250 kJ per kg.
mistakes.right: Just quoting numbers is ignored. Use the data to make a comparison, such as recycling needing far less energy than extracting from bauxite.
References to cost are ignored. Give a point about energy, raw materials, waste or greenhouse gas emissions.

worked_example.question:
Drinks cans are often made from aluminium.

4.0 kg of bauxite makes 1.0 kg of aluminium.
285 000 kJ of energy is needed to make 1.0 kg of aluminium from bauxite.

Aluminium can be recycled.

4.0 kg of recycled aluminium makes 3.8 kg of aluminium.
14 250 kJ of energy is needed to produce 1.0 kg of aluminium from recycled aluminium.

Describe and explain two advantages of recycling aluminium.

Use the information in the question in your answer.
answer_points: Recycling saves energy compared with extracting aluminium from bauxite: 14 250 kJ instead of 285 000 kJ per kg.
Recycling makes more aluminium from the same mass of starting material: 3.8 kg from 4.0 kg, compared with 1.0 kg from 4.0 kg of bauxite.
Other credited ideas: aluminium is not wasted, it is a finite resource, less waste or less greenhouse gas is produced, or less landfill is needed.
worked_example.tip: Any three marks. The answer must be comparative, and numbers alone are ignored.
